output.brief: Most likely this is one chance QC flag, not a fault in Analyzer B or the new reagent lot. Evidence: the repeat of the same material passed. The other two QC levels were fine. Sodium and chloride were fine. The Level 2 mean is unchanged after the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). The patient moving median is normal. Re-testing 43 samples on Analyzer A agreed within 0.20 mmol/L (mean +0.02). All scheduled QC ran on time, so the short-staffing theory is not supported. A sampling glitch is possible but unproven, so don't record it as confirmed. Ward 6's high potassiums look explained by the tube outage (more samples over 3 h old) and the renal overflow patients. Highs were split evenly between Analyzer A and B. I'm fairly sure, not certain. I did not collect any extra evidence. Sign off: return Analyzer B to service with no recall or quarantine, and do not widen the limits. Add extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Ask Ward 6 to send repeat samples on high results, and fix the tube station. Tell Dr Larkby the analyzers agree.
